mobile.schedules.cadence.every.note: Cadence phrase for a repeating schedule. {duration} is a formatted interval such as '1d' or '1h30m'; it is formatting, not prose, and is not translated in this slice.

mobile.schedules.cadence.left.note: Cadence with a bounded delivery budget. {cadence} is the already-rendered 'every …' phrase; {remaining} is a positive integer. The middle dot is a separator, keep it.

mobile.schedules.cadence.once.note: A schedule that fires once. One lower-case word; it replaces the whole cadence phrase.

mobile.schedules.cadence.spent.note: A repeating schedule whose delivery budget is used up. Says 'no deliveries left' rather than '0 left', which would promise a fire that cannot happen.

mobile.schedules.count.monitors.note: Monitor count. {count} is a non-negative integer and drives the plural category; # is that number.

mobile.schedules.count.wakes.note: Wake count. {count} is a non-negative integer and drives the plural category; # is that number.

mobile.schedules.due.ahead.note: A due instant still in the future. {label} is a relative duration such as '4m' or '1h30m' formatted by the client, not translated here.

mobile.schedules.due.overdue.note: A due instant already past. {label} is a relative duration such as '2h'. The word 'overdue' is the terminal's own word for this state; do not substitute 'late' or 'missed'.

mobile.schedules.empty.body.note: The both-families-empty explanation. Two sentences: what to do, then what a wake and a monitor each are. Only shown when BOTH stores read successfully and hold nothing.

mobile.schedules.empty.title.note: Empty-state heading. Short, no final full stop; the body sentence follows it.

mobile.schedules.empty_line.monitors.note: Shown under the monitors header when only the wakes family has content. A sentence with a full stop, unlike the header counters.

mobile.schedules.empty_line.wakes.note: Shown under the wakes header when only the monitors family has content. A sentence with a full stop, unlike the header counters.

mobile.schedules.gone.monitors.note: The conversation a monitor belonged to no longer exists on this machine, so nothing checks it. Deliberately distinct from the parked sentence: nothing can resume this.

mobile.schedules.gone.wakes.note: The conversation a wake belonged to no longer exists on this machine, so nothing fires it. Deliberately distinct from the parked sentence.

mobile.schedules.head.next.note: Entry head line: how many schedules, then the soonest future instant. {head} is an already-rendered count phrase; {label} is a relative duration. 'next' is dropped once the instant is overdue.

mobile.schedules.head.overdue.note: Entry head line when the soonest instant is already past. {head} is an already-rendered count phrase; {label} is a relative duration ending in the word 'overdue'. No forward-looking word here.

mobile.schedules.parked.monitors.note: The conversation is stopped, so its monitors pause. Monitors resume when the conversation next RUNS; opening it is not enough.

mobile.schedules.parked.wakes.note: The conversation is stopped, so its wakes are held. Wakes resume after its NEXT TURN; opening the conversation is not enough. Do not say 'when you open it'.

mobile.schedules.read_error.monitors.note: The monitor store could not be read. Must name the failed family and must never read like an empty list.

mobile.schedules.read_error.wakes.note: The wake store could not be read. Must name the failed family and must never read like an empty list.

mobile.schedules.read_unreachable.note: A read failed with no sentence of its own, i.e. a transport drop. The connection surface owns the cause; this only says the read did not happen.

mobile.schedules.show_less.monitors.note: Collapse control for the per-entry monitor disclosure. Shown only while expanded.

mobile.schedules.show_less.wakes.note: Collapse control for the per-entry wake disclosure. Shown only while expanded.

mobile.schedules.show_more.monitors.note: Expand control for hidden monitor rows. {hidden} is a positive integer driving the plural category; # is that number. The singular must read 'more monitor', not 'more monitors'.

mobile.schedules.show_more.wakes.note: Expand control for hidden wake rows. {hidden} is a positive integer driving the plural category; # is that number. The singular must read 'more wake', not 'more wakes'.

mobile.schedules.state.stale.note: One word replacing the due clock when the supervisor has given up on a wake. The terminal's own vocabulary for this state.

mobile.schedules.state.waiting.note: One word for an armed monitor with no recorded due time. Replaces the slot that would hold a due clock.

mobile.schedules.summary.monitors_armed.note: Monitors section header when every monitor is healthy. {count} is the number of monitor rows; no final full stop.

mobile.schedules.summary.monitors_attent.note: Monitors section header when at least one monitor needs attention. {broken} need attention out of {total} rows. Used instead of the armed counter so the header cannot contradict a row that reads disabled.

mobile.schedules.summary.wakes.note: Wakes section header. {count} counts wake ROWS, not conversations. No final full stop.

mobile.schedules.supervisor.not_running.note: The supervisor is installed but not running, so nothing will fire. Only shown when the probe could verify the supervisor's state.

mobile.schedules.supervisor.unsupported.note: This platform has no wake supervisor. Must win over the unverifiable sentence when both apply, because the platform is the real reason.

mobile.schedules.supervisor.unverifiable.note: The probe cannot speak for this store (sandbox or foreign store). Must not claim the supervisor is 'not running', which the probe never checked.

mobile.schedules.tail.failed.note: Failure count appended to a monitor row. {count} is a positive integer. Sits after the monitor's own health sentence.

mobile.schedules.truncated.note: The listing was capped. {shown} entries of {total} are rendered; the family select picks the noun so the sentence stays grammatical in locales where the noun inflects.
